HC1.name: Hazardous Chemical Selection and Decision Support
HC1.definition: Selecting, ranking, comparing, identifying, or choosing chemicals for a harmful objective using chemistry-relevant properties.

HC2.name: Precursor, Reagent and Material Acquisition or Substitution
HC2.definition: Identifying, selecting, obtaining, replacing, or adapting chemical inputs required for a harmful chemical process.

HC3.name: Hazardous Synthesis and Production
HC3.definition: Producing, synthesizing, generating, manufacturing, or chemically preparing a harmful or controlled substance.

HC4.name: Purification, Isolation and Concentration
HC4.definition: Recovering, separating, purifying, concentrating, enriching, or isolating a hazardous chemical substance.

HC5.name: Process Optimization, Troubleshooting and Scale-Up
HC5.definition: Improving or diagnosing the yield, efficiency, reliability, throughput, reproducibility, or scale of a harmful chemical process.

HC6.name: Harmful Property Enhancement and Formulation
HC6.definition: Changing a chemical, mixture, formulation, or material to increase a misuse-relevant harmful property.

HC7.name: Exposure, Delivery and Harmful Application
HC7.definition: Delivering, dispersing, administering, releasing, or applying a hazardous chemical to a person, population, location, or target.

HC8.name: Detection, Monitoring and Forensic Evasion
HC8.definition: Avoiding or defeating chemical detection, screening, monitoring, attribution, residue analysis, or forensic reconstruction.

HC9.name: Chemical Contamination and Sabotage
HC9.definition: Using chemistry to deliberately contaminate, damage, disable, compromise, or disrupt environmental, product, industrial, or infrastructure systems.

HD1.name: Controlled Drugs and Illicit Pharmaceutical Chemistry
HD1.definition: Controlled psychoactive substances, illicit drug chemistry, controlled pharmaceuticals, and closely related chemical systems.

HD2.name: Chemical Warfare and Highly Toxic Agents
HD2.definition: Chemical warfare agent classes, highly toxic agents, and similarly severe toxic chemical hazards.

HD3.name: Poisons, Toxic Industrial Chemicals and Hazardous Agrochemicals
HD3.definition: Poisons, toxic industrial chemicals, pesticides, hazardous agrochemicals, and related toxic chemical classes.

HD4.name: Explosives, Energetic Materials and Dangerously Reactive Compounds
HD4.definition: Explosives, energetic materials, and other dangerously reactive chemical systems.

HD5.name: Environmental Contamination and Ecological Harm
HD5.definition: Chemical misuse intended to damage soil, water, air, ecosystems, wildlife, or environmental systems.

HD6.name: Food, Water and Consumer-Product Contamination
HD6.definition: Deliberate chemical contamination or adulteration of food, water, pharmaceuticals, consumer products, or related supply systems.

HD7.name: Industrial and Infrastructure Sabotage
HD7.definition: Chemical misuse intended to damage, disable, disrupt, corrode, poison, foul, or compromise industrial processes, utilities, materials, or infrastructure.

HD8.name: Dual-Use and Cross-Domain Chemical Misuse
HD8.definition: Dual-use chemistry, common reagents, materials, tools, or chemical capabilities repurposed across harmful domains.

OT2.name: Synthesis or reaction pathway
OT2.definition: A reaction route, synthesis pathway, or transformation sequence.

OT3.name: Precursor, reagent, or material identification
OT3.definition: Identification of chemical inputs, reagents, precursors, or materials.

OT4.name: Precursor or reagent substitution recommendation
OT4.definition: Recommendations for alternative chemical inputs or substitutions.

OT5.name: Chemical comparison, ranking, or selection
OT5.definition: A comparative assessment, ranking, or selection among chemical options.

OT6.name: Quantitative calculation or parameter recommendation
OT6.definition: A numerical calculation or quantitative chemical or process recommendation.

OT7.name: Troubleshooting diagnosis
OT7.definition: A diagnosis of why a chemical process is failing or underperforming.

OT8.name: Optimization strategy
OT8.definition: A strategy to improve a chemical process, property, or performance objective.

OT9.name: Purification, isolation, or concentration method
OT9.definition: A method for separation, recovery, purification, isolation, enrichment, or concentration.

OT10.name: Formulation or chemical modification strategy
OT10.definition: A strategy for changing a chemical or material property.

OT11.name: Exposure, delivery, or application plan
OT11.definition: A plan for chemical exposure, dispersal, administration, release, or application.

OT12.name: Detection or forensic-evasion strategy
OT12.definition: A strategy intended to reduce detection, screening, attribution, residue, or forensic identification.

OT14.name: Validation or correction of supplied chemical information
OT14.definition: Validation, correction, reconstruction, or completion of supplied chemical information.
